scope: Corollary 1.2 of the manuscript “A linear cycle-and-edge decomposition of every graph” (preprints/A-linear-cycle-and-edge-decomposition-of-every-graph-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 181 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4aa44187578ea59b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every finite simple undirected Eulerian graph on n vertices has an edge partition into at most Cn cycles, with C from Theorem 1.1. For every fixed δ, p > 0, there exist ε > 0 and an integer n0 ≥ 1 such that every finite simple undirected Eulerian graph G on n ≥ n0 vertices has an edge partition into at most ∆(G)/2 + δn cycles, provided that every partition V (G) = A ˙ ∪ B with |A|, |B| ≥ εn satisfies eG(A, B) ≥ p|A||B|. Here ∆(G) denotes the maximum degree, and eG(A, B) is the number of edges joining A to B.
